location.geographicScope: MIT models countywide. One ZIP demonstration is not a precise ZIP-specific budget; do not extrapolate to other counties.

benchmarks.hhs: 2026 HHS administrative poverty guidelines (48 contiguous states and DC); not an actual living wage, and distinct from Census official statistical poverty thresholds.
benchmarks.mit: 2026 MIT Living Wage Calculator county family-type gross income needed for modeled basic necessities; one or two adults working full-time (2,080 hours per worker).
benchmarks.ratio: Annual MIT modeled gross income ÷ HHS guideline (descriptive model comparison, not benefits eligibility or individual judgment).

sources.organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.title: 2026 Poverty Guidelines
Living Wage Calculation for Bergen County, NJ

disclaimers: The HHS administrative guideline is not the Census official statistical poverty threshold.
MIT estimates a minimum adequate basket, not a complete comfort standard, and excludes savings, emergencies, leisure and retirement.
Families with one working and one nonworking adult are modeled with zero paid childcare expenses, excluding the second adult's unpaid time and opportunity cost.
2026 MIT costs represent county-level modeled budgets, not actual current rent listings or any household's expenses.
No user income or personal financial information is requested, stored or sent.
